title: Zariski and etale immediate specializations on universally catenary schemes
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings), and let $x,y\in X$ with $x$ in the closure of $y$. Let $Z$ be the closure of $y$ with its reduced induced structure, so that $\mathcal O_{Z,x}$ is a Noetherian local domain [def-weil-residue-field], and write $\dim$ for Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $\bar x$ be a geometric point over $x$ [def-weil-geometric-point] and $X_{(\bar x)}$ the strict localization [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. (a) If $\dim\mathcal O_{Z,x}=1$, then every point of $X_{(\bar x)}$ lying over $y$ has closure of dimension $1$ in $X_{(\bar x)}$. (b) If $X$ is universally catenary, meaning that it is covered by affine opens whose rings are universally catenary in the sense of [def-exc-excellent-ring] (in particular if $X$ is excellent), and some point of $X_{(\bar x)}$ lying over $y$ has closure of dimension $1$ in $X_{(\bar x)}$, then $\dim\mathcal O_{Z,x}=1$. Consequently, on a universally catenary Noetherian scheme, $y\rightsquigarrow x$ is an immediate specialization in the sense of [def-per-potential-dualizing] (codimension one in the strict localization at a geometric point over $x$) if and only if $\dim\mathcal O_{Z,x}=1$, and this does not depend on the choice of $\bar x$.

source.place: Expose XIV, Proposition 2.1.4 (Zariski immediate implies etale immediate; converse for universally catenary schemes), with Proposition 2.1.3 and Lemmas 2.1.5 and 2.1.6; used as in Expose XIV, proof of Proposition 2.2.2

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{W,x}$ for $W=\overline{\{y\}}_{\mathrm{red}}$ and put $Z=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-per-etale-immediate-component-criterion], $Z_{(\bar x)}=X_{(\bar x)}\times_X W$ and the closures of points above $y$ have the same dimensions in the two schemes. Thus both assertions may be proved on the local integral scheme $Z$, whose generic point is $y$ and closed point is $x$. In particular a one-dimensional closure above $y$ is a component of $Z_{(\bar x)}$; it need not be a component of $X_{(\bar x)}$.

source.place: Expose XIV, reduction preceding Proposition 2.1.3 and its proof, printed pp.209-210

proof.text: Assume $\dim A=1$. The only primes of the local domain $A$ are $(0)$ and its maximal ideal. By [lem-per-strict-localization-discrete-fibres], the fibre of $Z_{(\bar x)}\to Z$ over $y$ is nonempty and discrete. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples] for $Y=U=Z$ and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_A$, the ring of $Z_{(\bar x)}$ is the triples colimit $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] for $K=\kappa(\bar x)$; by the latter, its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m_A A^{\mathrm{sh}}$, so its fibre over $x$ has just the closed point $c$. For any $t$ over $y$, every specialization of $t$ other than $c$ is in that discrete fibre, hence equals $t$. Since a point of a local scheme specializes to its closed point, $\overline{\{t\}}=\{t,c\}$ with $t\ne c$. Its dimension is exactly one. Step 1 transfers this equality of dimensions to the ambient strict localization, proving (a) for every $t$.

For (b), choose an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $x$ with $R$ universally catenary. Write $A=R_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak q}$, where $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$ correspond to $y,x$, and $S=R\setminus\mathfrak q$. Every finite-type $A$-algebra $B$ is a quotient of $S^{-1}(R/\mathfrak p)[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. Contract its defining ideal to $(R/\mathfrak p)[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, obtaining $B=S^{-1}C$ with $C$ finite type over $R$. By [def-exc-excellent-ring], $C$ is catenary. Chains between fixed primes in $S^{-1}C$ correspond exactly to chains between their contractions in $C$: every intermediate prime avoids $S$. Their lengths and saturation are preserved, so $B$ is catenary. Thus $A=\mathcal O_{W,x}$ is universally catenary.

Construct $(H,\mathfrak m_AH)$ as the henselization of the pair $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ using [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization]. Its statement supplies a filtered colimit of etale $A$-algebras, a henselian pair, and $H/\mathfrak m_AH\simeq A/\mathfrak m_A=k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-factorization-criterion], $\mathfrak m_AH$ lies in every maximal ideal of $H$. Since its quotient is a field, it is the unique maximal ideal. Thus $H$ is henselian local, with residue field $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-noetherian-completion], $H$ is Noetherian and $\widehat H\simeq\widehat A$ for these maximal-ideal completions.

source.place: Expose XIV, final paragraph of Proposition 2.1.4 proof, printed p.211, through the application of Lemma 2.1.5

proof.text: Put $C=A^{\mathrm{sh}}$, with residue field $K=k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ and henselian local structure supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] to $H$ and the residue embedding $k\to K$, obtaining the unique local $A$-map $H\to C$. For any henselian local $H$-algebra $T$ with a prescribed embedding $K\to\kappa(T)$ over $k$, the same lemma gives a unique pointed $A$-map $C\to T$. This map is $H$-linear: the two composites $H\to T$ are equal by that lemma applied to the ind-etale $A$-algebra $H$, since both induce the prescribed map from $k$. The strict henselization of $H$ has exactly this pointed mapping property by the same lemma. Applying the two properties to each other gives inverse pointed $H$-maps, their composites being identities by uniqueness. Hence $C$ is the strict henselization of $H$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples], applied to $Y=Z$ and to $Y=\operatorname{Spec}H$ with the geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}H$ (both with $\kappa(\bar x)=K$), these triples colimits are the rings of $Z_{(\bar x)}$ and of $(\operatorname{Spec}H)_{(\bar x)}$; so $Z_{(\bar x)}=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is the strict localization of $\operatorname{Spec}H$.

proof.text: By Step 1 the assumed point with one-dimensional closure supplies a one-dimensional component of $\operatorname{Spec}C$. Apply [lem-per-henselian-component-dimension] to the Noetherian henselian local ring $H$ of Step 4 and its strict localization identified in Step 5. It follows that $\operatorname{Spec}H$ has a one-dimensional irreducible component.

source.place: Expose XIV, final paragraph of Proposition 2.1.4 proof, printed p.211, through the application of Lemma 2.1.5

proof.text: Apply the forward direction of [lem-per-completion-component-dimension] to $\operatorname{Spec}H$; no catenarity of $H$ is required. It gives a one-dimensional component of $\operatorname{Spec}\widehat H$. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-noetherian-completion], $\widehat H\simeq\widehat A$, so $\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$ has such a component. Now apply the converse of [lem-per-completion-component-dimension] to $A$, which Step 3 proved universally catenary. It follows that $\operatorname{Spec}A$ has a one-dimensional component. As $A$ is a domain, its only irreducible component is the whole spectrum, and hence $\dim\mathcal O_{W,x}=1$. This proves (b).

source.place: Expose XIV, final paragraph of Proposition 2.1.4 proof, printed p.211: easy direction of Lemma 2.1.6 for the henselization, equality of completions, then converse for the original local scheme

proof.text: Fix $\bar x$ and assume $\dim\mathcal O_{W,x}=1$. By [lem-per-strict-localization-discrete-fibres] the fibre of $X_{(\bar x)}\to X$ over $y$ contains a point $t$; by Step 2 its closure has dimension one. Let $a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'\to X_{(\bar x)}$ be a geometric point over $t$, $\Omega'$ an algebraic closure of $\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and put $\bar y=\rho_{\bar x}\circ a$, a geometric point of $X$ over $y$, with $\rho_{\bar x}$ the structural map [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. For an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\ni x$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples] writes the ring of $X_{(\bar x)}$ as a filtered colimit of etale, hence finitely presented, $R$-algebras, so $\rho_{\bar x}$ is ind-etale as required in [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance]. That lemma makes the functorial map $(X_{(\bar x)})_{(a)}\to X_{(\bar y)}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality] an isomorphism over $X$. Its inverse followed by the structural map $(X_{(\bar x)})_{(a)}\to X_{(\bar x)}$ is an $X$-map $X_{(\bar y)}\to X_{(\bar x)}$, i.e. a geometric specialization $\bar y\rightsquigarrow\bar x$. The isomorphism preserves closed points, and by clause 1 of the functoriality lemma the structural map sends the closed point to $t$. So the image of $\bar y$ is $t$, whose reduced closure has dimension one: the specialization is immediate in the sense of [def-per-potential-dualizing].

source.place: Expose XIV, Definitions 2.1.1-2.1.2 and the following remark (generizations etale immediate = images of points of the strict localization with one-dimensional closure), printed p.209; the identification of specializations with lifts is written out from the cited statements instead of the reference cited there

proof.text: Conversely, let $\bar y\rightsquigarrow\bar x$ be an immediate geometric specialization over $y\rightsquigarrow x$ [def-per-potential-dualizing]. Since it is an $X$-map, the image of $\bar y$ is a point of $X_{(\bar x)}$ over $y$, and its reduced closure has dimension one; Step 7 gives $\dim\mathcal O_{W,x}=1$. With Step 8 this is the required immediate-specialization criterion. If $y=x$, the only lift of $y$ in the strict localization is the closed point, with dimension-zero closure, while $\mathcal O_{W,x}$ is a field; neither condition holds. Steps 1-8 apply to an arbitrary choice of $\bar x$, and the ring $\mathcal O_{W,x}$ does not depend on that choice, so the equivalence is independent of $\bar x$.
